runs.name: Union Pacific Corporation
runs.entry: Price **$278.34** (close 2026-10-09, aggregator, flagged) x **594,075,498 shares** (10-Q cover as of 2026-07-17, 0000100885-26-000250; one class; issued 1,113,359,575 less treasury = 593,957,035 at 2026-06-30; no 8-K or prospectus after the 10-Q) = cap **$165,355M**; sovereign **5.60%** (UST 30Y par, 2026-10-09). Pending: the Norfolk Southern merger (agreement 2025-07-28; 1 UNP share plus $88.82 cash per NSC share, about 225M new shares and about $20B of new borrowing; STB approval pending at 2026-06-30, 10-Q Note 18; buybacks paused), valued beside and not in the central figure. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs. Q1 IN (one integrated network, one reportable segment). Q2 IN (no second western railroad can be built; core pricing gains held in every volume-down year, 2009, 2015, 2016, 2019, 2020 and 2023; returns read on historical cost, replacement cost carried to Q3 and Q4). Q3 against (capital spending 1.3 to 2.3 times depreciation every year 2015-2025, compulsory; about 14% to 17% pre-tax on historical cost). Q4 against, no STOP (the filer's own words: depreciation at replacement prices "would be substantially greater than historically reported amounts"; the 40% return on equity made by buybacks and debt; 2025 EPS growth leaned on land sales and tax items; ten balance sheets 2016 to mid-2026: no goodwill, debt $15.0B to $33.3B, treasury stock $58.8B, $70.3B paid out 2016-2025 against about $51B of owner cash). Q5 integrity IN, ability weighs for (no investigation, restatement or control weakness found; independent chairman; three-year EPS targets and adjusted EPS weighed, no doubt raised). Q6 against, no STOP (buybacks by share count, never by price, yearly averages $143.70 to $240.51, every year above the Q7 bottom and from 2021 above its top; the NSC case rests on $2.75B of "annualized synergies" stated as EBITDA; not all-stock, so the narrower STOP does not arise). **Q7 OUT on the floor:** no case earns about ten percent at $278.34 (expected return 2.6% to 4.5% by case, the most generous included, below the 5.60% long Treasury). Owner cash (operating cash less stock pay, all capital spending and finance-lease principal) FY2021-FY2025 $5,902M, $5,552M, $4,601M, $5,729M, $5,321M, mean $5,421M, **$6,401M** before interest, falling 1.71% a year; literal window central (neither end year aberrational on the filer's description); inverted by specific (e): maintenance-only no-growth case the top, all-spending at the shrinking rate the bottom. Net debt $28,213M at 2026-06-30. Range **$120.64-$162.31** all-equity (equity-only $133.15-$180.33), width 1.35 to 1; cycle-average growth sensitivity 3.82% beside, $213.14, 4.53%; fair **$59.30** all-equity ($88.94 equity-only); with NSC as if closed, no synergy, $80.81-$115.58 a share (all-spending cases), value per share down a fifth to a third on the deal's filed terms. Q8 to Q12 not reached. Competitors: the 10-K names one rail rival, BNSF (files a 10-K); trucks, barges, ships and pipelines named only as classes. UNP's operating ratio beat BNSF's every year 2014-2025 (59.8% against 65.6% in 2025; BNSF carries Berkshire's purchase accounting, flattering UNP by an unstated amount); both lost units, both spend about 1.5 times depreciation. Strongest evidence against: volume 12% below its 2014 peak, coal revenue $4,127M to $1,786M, growth from price not units. Could not get: NSC's growth-maintenance split; finance-lease principal before 2019; a value range as of each buyback date. Analyst's framework gaps for the operator: (1) Q2's "ordinary returns" names no base; on historical cost a railroad passes, on replacement cost the speakers' own word is "a pittance" (M2024-058) and Q2 would close OUT for every railroad; (2) specific (e) does not say which series sets the bottom when owner-cash growth is negative on every series (the all-spending series used); (3) specific (a) gives no test for a filer's neutral description of an unusual end year (FY2021 here; the box does not turn on it); (4) the overnight brief's competitor rule yielded one rival where Q2 asks for competitors in the plural. Contamination declared by the analyst: a directory listing of Test Runs/ showed four other run file names of 2026-10-11 (SHOP, SPGI, TECH, TXN) and the session context showed the TXN fold's commit subject; two ledger rows name Union Pacific (M2021-018, M2021-038), declared and weighed as the speakers' view at their date; none of the blind-listed files opened. Ten commits (eff748e8 to 71ada82a), one per question. Dispatcher quote check: 89 quoted fragments beside ids, 64 matched by the script; the 25 others are filer quotes attributed to the filer or window artifacts where the fragment belongs to an earlier citation (spot-checked by hand: M2025-043, M2000-014, M2016-092, M2010-090, M2024-058), and one capitalization and elision difference in M2005-020 ("You learn a lot about [...] the durability", the row reading "you learn a lot about – the durability"); no slip found; recorded, not fixed. v4.1 bands retired at the fold; v5 fair-price alert armed at $59.30. Position note filled at the fold. check_framework PASS.
runs.narr: Q7 OUT on the floor at $278.34: range $120.64-$162.31 all-equity on the literal FY2021-FY2025 window, owner cash falling 1.71% a year, fair $59.30; Q1 and Q2 IN on the unbuildable western network and pricing held through every volume-down year, Q3, Q4 and Q6 against on compulsory spending above depreciation, a 40% ROE made by buybacks and debt, buybacks above any computed value, and the pending Norfolk Southern merger, which as if closed lowers value per share by a fifth to a third without its synergies. Four framework gaps reported, chief among them that Q2's ordinary-returns test names no base (historical cost passes a railroad, replacement cost fails it).
runs.fair_label: UNP at/below $59.30: the fair price on the all-equity basis of the blind v5 purchase run of 2026-10-11 (Test Runs/2026-10-11 Run - UNP Union Pacific.md; OUT at Q7 at $278.34; $88.94 equity-only; literal FY2021-FY2025 window; standalone, the Norfolk Southern merger pending, $80.81-$115.58 a share as if closed). A prompt to re-run Q7, never a verdict.
